biggest_gap.title: No clean-clone verify can pass on a busy machine: the dotnet stage stops at its test-group partition check because the `dotnet test --list-tests` output it reads comes out interleaved
biggest_gap.detail: p09 itself now does its job. It beats Odoo on add-a-custom-field-and-filter on every metric. Round 2's gaps are fixed: a select default is kept at creation, option values keep acronyms (EXW, FOB, CIF), a descending sort puts values first, and text and number fields can be grouped. My isolation and permission attacks found nothing, and every fault I planted was caught. But the round has no full passing verify, and none of the roughly 1,100 .NET tests ran in any of my 5 runs. In build/verify-inside.sh (p00 r20, commit 4f22209d), list_tests runs `dotnet test Erp.slnx --list-tests` (and the per-group listings) and keeps the lines starting with four spaces. The test hosts of several projects write to the same pipe at once, so two test names sometimes land on one line, for example 'Erp.Kernel.Tests.SecurityTests.Email_validation(value: "a@b", valid: False)    Erp.Modules.Reports.Tests.RenderingTests.Mixed_text_is_ordered_as_a_reader_expects(...)'. The diff of tests-all.txt against tests-groups.txt then fails, and the stage exits 141 after about 125 s. It happened in all 5 runs, at load 58 to 122 at the moment of the check, each time on different pairs, on either side of the diff. The integrator's alone run of this merge passed, and p00 r20's critic verify got past the check while mine failed, so this is a race that load makes likely, not a product fault of p09. The likely fix (for p00): list one project at a time, or read --list-tests per test assembly, or match full lines and split on runs of 4 or more spaces. Never weaken or drop the partition check. Until then any critic verify beside another verify is likely to fail before testing anything. Owner: p00-foundation.
biggest_gap.evidence: To reproduce, run ./erp verify on a clean clone of ee489aba while another verify runs (load above about 50), then read '[dotnet] The test groups are not every test exactly once:' in the log. Audit trail (p09 surface): a single-select custom field's history shows the stored option value, not its label, in both languages. A change shows 'Customer segment: keyAccount → government' in English and 'شريحة العميل: keyAccount → government' on the Arabic screen, instead of 'Key account → Government' and 'حساب رئيسي → حكومي' (ui/en-history-select-values.jpg, ui/ar-history-select-values.jpg; api/seg.mjs reproduces it). Lookups show the record's name and numbers show 2 decimals correctly. Custom dates show as 2027-12-31 in history, while the list shows 31 Dec 2027.

Custom fields screen (p09): for a date field, 'Default for new records' is the browser's native date input, which shows US mm/dd/yyyy (01/31/2027). Typing 2027-01-31 turns into year 70131 and the save is refused. In Arabic, a default typed in Arabic-Indic digits (٢٠٢٧-٠١-٣١) is silently dropped: the field saves with default null and no message (ui/en-date-default-us-format.jpg; scripts ui/scripts/en5d.mjs and ar5.mjs). The contact form's custom date takes typed yyyy-mm-dd in either set of digits.

Group by a custom date per month or year (new in r3) exists only in the API (groupBy=cfX.month or .year); the column menu groups dates by day only. It is slow over 100,008 contacts: 16.7 s by month and 9.1 s by year, against 1.1 s by day, at load 15 to 23 (api/timing-out.txt). value_date_trunc wraps value_date once per row. Odoo groups dates by month by default.

[route: p06-forms] In Arabic exports (CSV, Excel and PDF), a lookup custom field shows the target's English name ('Gulf Glass Co.') where the Arabic form shows 'شركة الخليج للزجاج'. The built-in Organisation column does the same, so the cause is the report engine (ui/export-1.pdf, ui/export-3.csv, ui/export-5.xlsx are the Arabic exports). The English CSV also leaves Name blank for a contact that has only an Arabic name, while the list shows it (ui/export-2.csv).

[route: p05-list-search] The list's Filter… dialog uses native <input type=number> and <input type=date> (kernel/lists/parts.tsx:310). On the Arabic screen, Arabic-Indic digits typed there (sent by Playwright as text input) are not taken: the filter silently stays off and 100,008 rows remain (ui/ar-filter-arabic-digits-empty.jpg). With Latin digits it works in both languages (2 rows, chip 'at least 200,000.00'). The product's form fields accept Arabic-Indic digits.

Adding a required custom field with a default stops any existing record from being saved in its form until someone fills the field. The form sends null for the empty field, while the API applies the default when the key is absent. With 100,000 contacts, a required field added later means every old contact needs the field filled before the first edit.

API documentation: OpenAPI describes customFields generically and points to GET /api/customfields/fields; a field added by the workspace (cfInsuranceCover31) is not named in /api/openapi/v1.json, signed in or not. This is unchanged since r1 (api/openapi-signed-in.json).

Still open since round 1: a number custom field has no currency, rate or base amount, so a money custom field cannot follow CLAUDE.md rule 2. Import could not be judged: there is no contact import yet (p14). Lookup custom fields cannot be sorted or grouped (400). This is by design in the list contract gate; Odoo groups by many-to-one properties.

Fixed since round 2 and still fixed: the select default is kept when chosen at creation (Incoterm: default FOB; Shipping line: default maersk, by keyboard in Arabic). Option values keep acronyms (EXW, FOB, CIF, MSC). A descending sort by a custom date gives 2026-12-31 first. Group by custom text and number now works. Print and export with custom columns and custom-field filters work in PDF, CSV and Excel, in both languages (2 rows, Arabic option labels in the Arabic files).

Works end to end by keyboard in English and Arabic: adding text, number (2 decimals, required, default 1500.25 or ١٢٠٠٫٥), date, yes/no, single select and lookup fields. Contact form values are saved and read back exactly through the API: 250000.75, 2027-12-31 (also typed as ٢٠٢٧-١٢-٣١), true, the lookup id with its name, and the text. Column chooser, header-menu filter, group by day, search on a searchable text field, and labelled history entries all work. Field definitions and values are audited in audit.entries with actor, and old and new values per custom_fields.<key>.

Performance: custom-field filters over 100,008 contacts answered in 34 to 340 ms through the API at load about 12 to 28: select eq, text contains, date range, yes/no, an AND of select-in and yes/no, and number ge. Sort by a custom date took 2.0 s and a deep skip of 50,000 took 1.2 s (api/timing-out.txt).

[route: p00-foundation] As in round 2, G1HttpIsolationTests walks each list's registered static columns, not a workspace's custom columns (sort, filter, groupBy and print columns by cf key). Today, forced RLS, the process-state gate and the tenant-setting source rule cover it: my static-cache and header-switch plants were caught by those rules, not by the HTTP attack.
